performance.title: The flagship delivers operational value; establish its full return
performance.subtitle: M1 Northstar leadership review 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31
performance.statement: 97,488 automated tickets demonstrate a meaningful operating footprint
performance.body: The CSV records 789,563 model requests and 68.0% automation across the month. The final week reached 70.1% automation, compared with 65.8% in the opening week. The operating opportunity is to absorb routine demand while experienced staff handle exceptions.
performance.conclusion: First assess flagship benefits against implementation and ongoing costs. Use that evidence to decide whether expansion is worth funding.
performance.footer: Source: supplied Northstar case brief and synthetic daily metrics. Reporting period 2026-08-01 to 2026-08-31. The reported handle-time and CSAT benefits come from the brief. Daily data establish in-month progress, not a new pre/post study. Automation counts do not establish verified resolution.

cost.title: Model traffic grew; cost per automated ticket rose
cost.subtitle: M2 Opening 7 days versus final 7 days 2026-08-01–2026-08-07 and 2026-08-25–2026-08-31
cost.conclusion: Recorded spend: $1,213.12; full operating cost is not yet established. Set owners and deadlines for remaining issues, then prioritize improvements by customer benefit and cost.
cost.footer: Operational notes in the CSV provide incident context. Proposed controls: atomic policy releases and peak-load tests. Errors are request-weighted, automation uses ticket counts; other rates and latency quantiles are daily means. Spend is treated as inference for planning, not total support cost.

readiness.title: Essentials' value proposition favors fast, efficient support
readiness.subtitle: M3 / M4 Expansion hypotheses Earliest windows from approved kickoff
phases: Fast, low-effort resolution; bot-led routine support with human exceptions.
Policy owner signs off; isolation and peak-load tests pass.
Fashion shoppers; accessible pricing and promotional choice.
Confidence in fit and exchanges; automate facts, assist on exceptions.
Fresh catalog and exception tests pass; operations lead accepts the workflow.
Considered home-goods buyers; higher purchase commitment.
Suitability and delivery confidence; system lookups plus specialists.
Read-only connectors pass; data freshness and fallback have named owners.
Premium shoppers; personalized service is part of the proposition.
Discretion and continuity; concierge-led service with AI assistance.
Concierge owner accepts assist scope, policy boundaries and quality results.
readiness.note: *Readiness gates govern each window. Luxe is assist-only. Reorder if another brand offers better value and readiness.
readiness.conclusion: One live pilot at a time; preparation runs in parallel. Week 4 acceptance is provisional until final recontacts mature in Week 5; unmet gates shift dates.
readiness.footer: Source: scenario brand profiles. Customer preferences, pricing positions and windows are assumptions; the flagship CSV contains no brand-level customer research. Test acceptance, eligible demand and full cost before scaling.

decisions.title: Confirm flagship value, then authorize a bounded pilot
decisions.subtitle: M5 Proposed decisions Days start at this review; pilot weeks start at approved kickoff
decision_boxes: Compare verified support benefits with implementation, labor, integration and ongoing costs. Cash ROI and payback are not yet established.
Seven representative days meeting agreed response, completion and CSAT limits versus matched manual support; no severe unresolved policy/isolation failure. Final recontacts mature in Week 5.
Routine order, product and policy support; a 20,000-ticket ceiling. Stage traffic only after policy, quality and fallback checks pass.
timeline: Agree customer service needs; assign owners for the flagship benefit and full-cost assessment
Validate catalog and peak-load safeguards; explain rising requests per ticket
Review flagship value and sustained service; decide whether to fund Essentials
Escalate missed commitments; act immediately on material customer harm
decisions.owners: Owners: Northstar VP CX and VP Engineering. The Fireworks delivery lead owns integration. The policy owner signs off before live traffic.
decisions.conclusion: Agree the owners and deadlines now. Fund the pilot when the flagship value assessment and Essentials readiness support the investment; extend review if evidence is insufficient.
decisions.footer: All expansion brands, stakeholder roles, timing and commercial estimates are planning assumptions. Proposed dates are not existing commitments. Review at least seven representative days of service; elapsed time alone does not establish readiness. Pilot Week 4 acceptance is provisional; final recontacts mature in Week 5.
